extracted.intended_audience: literary scholars, magazine editors, bibliographers, and researchers of short fiction
extracted.subtask_description: A historical bibliometric framework for assessing short-story quality and periodical performance (Jan–Oct 1918), including an asterisk-based distinction system, exclusions, thresholds for inclusion in rankings, and tie-breaking/adjustment guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asterisk distinction system
rubrics_metrics.description: One, two, and three asterisks are employed to indicate relative distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-asterisk stories are of somewhat permanent literary value. (Uses 1–3 asterisks to signal degrees of distinction.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of reprints / inclusion of translations
rubrics_metrics.description: The table excludes reprints, but not translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All reported counts and percentages omit reprinted items; translations are counted as original contributions for the purposes of the tables and rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Averages of American periodicals published during the ten-month period before November 1, 1918 (January to October, 1918).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All counts, percentages, and derived rankings are calculated only for stories published within this ten-month window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion threshold for ranked magazine list
rubrics_metrics.description: The ranking (by percentage) considers the nineteen periodicals which have published during the period over twenty-one stories and which have exceeded an average of 15 per cent in stories of distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magazines must meet both: >21 stories published in the period AND >15% distinctive stories to be included in the primary ranked list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking metrics — percentage vs number
rubrics_metrics.description: Magazines are ranked both BY PERCENTAGE OF DISTINCTIVE STORIES and BY NUMBER OF DISTINCTIVE STORIES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two complementary ranking perspectives are presented: a rate-based ranking (percentage of distinctive stories among that magazine's output) and a volume-based ranking (absolute count of distinctive stories). Both are used to evaluate periodical performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-asterisk stories list criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The following periodicals have published during the same period eight or more "two-asterisk stories."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate listing highlights magazines that reached a threshold (≥8) in the mid-level (two-asterisk) distinction category; these lists exclude reprints but include translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-asterisk stories list criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The following periodicals have published during the same period four or more "three-asterisk stories."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate listing highlights magazines that reached the high-level (three-asterisk) threshold (≥4) during the period; again excluding reprints but not translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie-breaking procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Ties in the above lists have been decided by taking relative rank in other lists into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When two magazines tie on a given metric, their positions are resolved by comparing their relative positions across the other presented rankings (e.g., if tied by percent, consult the number list, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation-adjustment caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: The New York Tribune and The Stratford Journal gain their high place chiefly through translations of foreign stories, and allowance should be made for this in any qualitative estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers and evaluators should consider the source composition (original vs translated) when making qualitative judgments about a magazine's standing; high rank due mainly to translations may warrant adjustment in qualitative assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-year summary exclusion of reprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Reprints have not been taken into account in the last two lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the comparative four-year summaries and the lists of magazines leading over multiple years, reprinted stories are omitted from counts to avoid inflating long-term totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbol notation for prior-year representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodicals represented in this list during 1915 as well are indicated by an asterisk. Periodicals represented in this list during 1916 are indicated by a dagger, and during 1917 by the sign §.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of symbols flags continuity of representation across prior years, which informs longitudinal interpretation of a periodical's performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation: exclusion/inclusion clarifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The table excludes reprints, but not translations. The list excludes reprints, but not translations. (repeated clarifications in the source).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This repeated emphasis signals that counting rules consistently treat translations as publications to be measured, while reprints are systematically excluded in all enumerations and rankings.
